judged_text: updateEvent's fallback changed from event.destinationCalendar?.externalId to event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId, which when externalCalendarId is falsy searches for calendars whose externalId equals undefined. Any updateEvent call without an externalCalendarId now resolves selectedCalendar to undefined, so calendar.events.update is invoked with an undefined calendarId and the Google API call fails — previously the update targeted the destination calendar's externalId and succeeded.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the `updateEvent` calendar selection logic was changed to:
```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```
When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (e.g., `null/undefined`), this performs a `.find(... === externalCalendarId)` which effectively searches for `cal.externalId === undefined/null`, typically returning `undefined`. This removes the prior fallback (`event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`), so calls that don’t provide `externalCalendarId` no longer reliably pick the destination calendar and can end up passing an undefined/incorrect `calendarId` to `calendar.events.update`, breaking updates for existing bookings/references that lack `externalCalendarId`.
